# Plan 13: Ash Meridian Diplomacy and Late-Game Coalition

**Status:** Starter expansion wave plus Continuation Wave 2; documentation-only, premise-gated, and not an implementation claim. **Wave target:** Plans 13–16 synchronized multi-edit, with distinct mechanics, story content, locations, shelter lore, character arcs, factions, and late-game material.

**Domain:** faction diplomacy, coalition politics, treaty pressure, and late-game alliance formation.

**Current-owner boundary:** Candidate work must route through DiplomaticSummitSystem, the canonical faction standing authority, relationship and radio owners, CampaignState, ShelterArchiveSystem, and existing quest/campaign routing. No second faction ledger, relationship store, map graph, shelter counter, ending resolver, legacy store, or parallel save section may be created.

## Scope and non-duplication contract

This plan treats a treaty shard under soot, a brass envoy seal, a lantern map with three routes, and a green-bound coalition ledger as authored anchors for a new playable layer. They are not assumed to exist in the shipped catalog. The current source audit must verify IDs, consumers, host construction, save registration, and live claims before any row becomes implementation-ready. The proposed signals — standing drift, envoy trust, treaty age, public rumor, route leverage, security tension, and coalition readiness — are read models or content prerequisites until an owner is named.

The proposed cast and political vocabulary are deliberately provisional: Ash Meridian Compact, Glass Orchard Syndicate, Quiet Foundry League, Long-Wake Assembly, and Sable Relay. The late-game proposal is a proposed late-game Meridian Assembly that can become a major regional power only if current faction IDs, standing sinks, and ending branches prove there is no existing equivalent. Existing diplomacy, standing, relationship, map, roster, archive, campaign, ending, and legacy behavior remains authoritative. Where an existing system already expresses a requested outcome, this plan supplies content, projection, UX, or a bridge rather than a replacement.

## Nine synchronized expansion passes

### Pass 1: Treaty Shard Records

#### Field 1 — Canon, premise, and evidence boundary

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Keep the proposed coalition as a projection over the current diplomacy and standing owners. A treaty record can describe clauses, signatories, guarantees, expiry, and violations, while every standing delta must pass through the canonical faction port. The premise gate must confirm the existing summit and treaty IDs before new content is authored. In this pass, the clause is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 2 — Player loop and moment-to-moment decisions

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Make diplomacy a playable weekly loop: hear a rumor, choose an envoy, prepare a concession, travel to a neutral site, negotiate a clause, and live with the next day's reaction. The player should compare food, fuel, medical stock, route safety, and survivor trust without opening a second resource ledger. A failed meeting leaves an authored consequence record rather than silently resetting relations. In this pass, the coalition is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 3 — New mechanic and systemic rules

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Use a coalition readiness score as a derived view, not a new campaign truth. It can combine existing standing, treaty stability, route access, shared threats, and witness confidence. Thresholds should unlock content packets such as joint patrols, shared workshops, or a late-game council scene; they must not directly mutate combat or faction war without an existing command route. In this pass, the rumor is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 4 — Locations, shelter spaces, and environmental lore

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Treat the Meridian sites as proposal locations with clear visual and narrative jobs. The Exchange is a crowded archive of scales and stamped copper; the cisterns are fragrant with bitter leaves; Foundry Hall rings after dark; the signal yard blinks through ash; Relay steps hold the quietest negotiations. Verify location IDs and map ownership before adding any POI. In this pass, the treaty is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 5 — Character personalities, factions, and late-game cast

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Give the cast conflicting habits instead of interchangeable quest voices. Mara counts pauses in a conversation, Oren avoids promises he cannot carry, Ilyra uses plant metaphors to test sincerity, and Tomas answers every threat with a repair estimate. Their trust should be a read from existing relationship records plus authored scene flags, never a parallel affection store. In this pass, the coalition is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 6 — Authored data, content schema, and catalog validation

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Author content as snake_case JSON candidates with explicit schema_version, stable IDs, owner, trigger, prerequisites, effects, failure text, and archive tags. Candidate IDs should be namespaced by plan and rejected if they collide with current catalogs. Faction names remain proposals until the catalog census confirms they are not aliases for live factions. In this pass, the coalition is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 7 — Persistence, deterministic replay, and migration seams

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Treat negotiations as deterministic. A seeded keyed roll may resolve an uncertain witness or weather delay, but inputs must include campaign seed, summit ID, round, and clause ID. Capture active summit state, treaty status, agenda index, and processed consequence IDs through the existing save-section seam before any host presentation is claimed. In this pass, the coalition is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 8 — Host routing, UI scaffolding, UX, accessibility, and performance

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. The UI slice needs a readable treaty board, a compact envoy roster, and a consequence preview that states what is known and what is uncertain. Controller focus must move from clause list to delegate list to commit and back. Radio, journal, and archive surfaces should consume emitted facts and dispose listeners on route changes. In this pass, the rumor is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 9 — Storylines, prose, side quests, and consequence writing

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Write side quests that make diplomacy physical: carry a dry seal through a flooded culvert, recover a missing witness, choose whether to publish a forged clause, or host a meal where an insult is repaired. Each scene needs a quiet prose beat and a systemic consequence. The player can protect dignity, stockpile leverage, or spend scarce goodwill for a faster pact. In this pass, the clause is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 10 — Verification, rollout order, rollback, and handoff

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Verification starts with premise checks against live faction IDs, treaty APIs, save sections, and current integration claims. The first safe slice is one neutral meeting, one clause, one emitted treaty fact, one archive projection, and one reload assertion. Rollback is deletion of unclaimed candidate rows and scene references; no production authority should need a compensating migration. In this pass, the envoy is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

**Pass 1 receipt:** The Treaty Shard Records pass is complete as a planning artifact when its ten fields have current evidence, one owner each, a bounded first slice, and an explicit unresolved question list. No production change is implied.

The archive remains a projection of events owned elsewhere and must not become a shadow campaign history. Keep the proposed coalition as a projection over the current diplomacy and standing owners. A treaty record can describe clauses, signatories, guarantees, expiry, and violations, while every standing delta must pass through the canonical faction port. The premise gate must confirm the existing summit and treaty IDs before new content is authored. Author content as snake_case JSON candidates with explicit schema_version, stable IDs, owner, trigger, prerequisites, effects, failure text, and archive tags. Candidate IDs should be namespaced by plan and rejected if they collide with current catalogs. Faction names remain proposals until the catalog census confirms they are not aliases for live factions.

## Twelve story and side-quest packets

### Story packet 1: The Brass Seal

Mara finds a seal stamped with a faction that says it has no surviving office. The player can return it, expose the forgery, or use it to buy one quiet meeting. The prose should linger on warm metal in a cold hand and the cost of being believed. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 2: Three Lanterns

Oren carries three lamps through ash weather, each promised to a different witness. Which light reaches the Exchange determines who feels invited and who feels managed. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 3: The Orchard Debt

Ilyra offers fruit cuttings for medical stock, but the cuttings carry a history of a burned grove. A generous bargain can still sound like conquest if the player ignores the story. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 4: Foundry Silence

Tomas asks the shelter to stop broadcasting for one night so a rival can speak. The choice trades short-term security for a chance at a public apology. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 5: The Unnamed Clause

A treaty draft has one blank line where a family protection clause should be. Filling it costs leverage; leaving it blank creates a quiet future failure. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 6: Rumor House

A child repeats a rumor before the envoy arrives. The player can punish the source, trace the fear, or let the rumor travel and watch the public mood shift. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 7: Witness at the Cistern

A witness will only testify beside running water. The scene turns route preparation into a conversation about who gets to call a place neutral. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 8: Green Ledger Night

The ledger keeper reads names aloud and waits after each one. The player can correct the record, protect a debtor, or accept that the coalition begins with an omission. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 9: Broken Guarantee

A guarantee exchange fails when a survivor refuses to leave the shelter. The player must choose consent, treaty stability, or a public breach that cannot be hidden. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 10: The Quiet Foundry Vote

Foundry workers vote with tools placed on a table. The prose describes each object and lets the player infer the faction mood without a giant meter. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 11: Relay Weather

The Sable Relay loses the sky for a day. A hand-delivered message can arrive sooner, but its wording becomes the sender's responsibility. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 12: Meridian Dawn

The late coalition assembles at dawn. The final beat is not a victory speech; it is a shared list of repairs and a chair left open for the absent. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

## Ten systemic integration bridges

### Campaign bridge

Route the feature through current campaign state and existing quest flags. The bridge consumes standing drift, envoy trust, treaty age, public rumor, route leverage, security tension, and coalition readiness as derived evidence and emits one named fact for campaign routing; it does not add a second campaign clock. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Faction bridge

Route standing or faction consequences through the canonical faction authority. Candidate groups such as Ash Meridian Compact, Glass Orchard Syndicate, Quiet Foundry League, Long-Wake Assembly, and Sable Relay remain provisional until IDs, aliases, and sinks are verified. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Relationship bridge

Read relationship and trust through the current survivor owner. A scene flag can remember a beat, but pair affinity, decay, grief, and consent remain with the existing system. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Exploration bridge

Use current map, expedition, vehicle, and route seams for the Meridian Exchange, the Glass Orchard cisterns, Quiet Foundry Hall, Long-Wake signal yard, and Sable Relay steps. New route or location content must project onto existing discovery and travel state. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Shelter bridge

Use current facilities, expansion, power, water, needs, and archive consumers. A lore packet may describe a room, but it cannot create a duplicate room capacity or resource balance. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Data bridge

Add only schema-valid, snake_case candidate data with explicit references and migration notes. Validate IDs, ranges, localization keys, and consumer reachability before writing more volume. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Save bridge

Capture only non-recomputable authored progress and processed IDs in the selected owner. Require round-trip and legacy fixture evidence before calling a slice persistent. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Determinism bridge

Use seeded keyed inputs with stable ordering. Paired replay should match outcomes, archive IDs, event order, and epilogue selection across save/load. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### UI bridge

Expose existing commands with truthful state, focus-safe navigation, readable copy, and disposal. Panels, radio, journal, and archive views remain adapters over facts. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Performance bridge

Bound catalog loading, archive queries, route previews, and long prose. Prefer indexed projections and batched records; document a budget and a rollback path if the slice exceeds it. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

## First safe implementation packet

1. Re-run the premise census for DiplomaticSummitSystem, the canonical faction standing authority, relationship and radio owners, CampaignState, ShelterArchiveSystem, and existing quest/campaign routing and attach current file paths, APIs, data IDs, save sections, host constructors, and claims from the live ledger.
2. Select one small vertical slice built from the anchors a treaty shard under soot, a brass envoy seal, a lantern map with three routes, and a green-bound coalition ledger; include one player command, one canonical mutation or read projection, one visible result, one archive/journal fact, and one reload assertion.
3. Add candidate content only after schema and localization review. Keep the proposed names Ash Meridian Compact, Glass Orchard Syndicate, Quiet Foundry League, Long-Wake Assembly, and Sable Relay and the Meridian Exchange, the Glass Orchard cisterns, Quiet Foundry Hall, Long-Wake signal yard, and Sable Relay steps tagged as provisional until catalogs confirm them.
4. Run focused static and contract checks, then a deterministic paired replay if the slice consumes seeded variation. No full suite is requested by this planning wave.
5. Hand off the exact files, owner seam, evidence, limits, and rollback instructions. A plan completion receipt is not a production integration receipt.

## Acceptance and stop lines

Acceptance requires: current premise evidence; one authoritative mutation owner; candidate data that passes schema and reference review; explicit save and deterministic behavior where state exists; a reachable host route or a clearly labeled content-only row; accessible UI copy; bounded performance; and a handoff note. Stop immediately if the proposed major factions or systems duplicate an existing faction, ending, legacy, map, relationship, archive, or campaign authority, or if ownership is unclear. Report the blocker rather than improvising a parallel system.

## Documentation receipt

The starter wave and Continuation Wave 2 now provide a ten-field scaffold, twenty synchronized passes, high-volume content banks, twenty-four story packets, twenty bridge notes, and bounded first-safe-slice handoffs. They do not modify Core, Godot scenes, production JSON, tests, or the live integration ledger.

All material is documentation-only, premise-gated, and designed to extend current owners rather than fork them.

## Twelve new story and side-quest packets

### Story packet 13: The Witness Ledger

A witness asks to be paid in dry batteries, not food, because power keeps a name alive. The player can honor the request, negotiate a substitute, or expose the demand. The packet requires an entry condition, player choice, existing owner call, failure or refusal route, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Keep the prose playable and concise enough for localization, while allowing the mechanic and data contract to carry the actual systemic change.

The public clause hearing begins only when a cracked bell rings twice. A missing second ring forces the player to decide whether silence counts as dissent. Route all consequences for Ash Meridian Compact, Glass Orchard Syndicate, Quiet Foundry League, Long-Wake Assembly, and Sable Relay through the canonical faction standing or diplomacy owner after ID and alias checks. The evidence packet includes one source path, one data row or content key, one input/output example, and one stop condition.

### Relationship bridge

Read trust, affinity, grief, consent, and decay from current survivor systems. Scene progress may remember a beat without becoming a relationship ledger. The evidence packet includes one source path, one data row or content key, one input/output example, and one stop condition.

### Map and route bridge

Project Meridian Exchange, Glass Orchard cisterns, Quiet Foundry Hall, Long-Wake signal yard, and Sable Relay steps onto current cartography, expedition, vehicle, weather, and route seams. A route proposal is not a new world graph. The evidence packet includes one source path, one data row or content key, one input/output example, and one stop condition.

### Shelter bridge

Use current facilities, expansion, power, water, needs, duty, archive, and memorial owners. Lore cannot invent a second room capacity or resource balance. The evidence packet includes one source path, one data row or content key, one input/output example, and one stop condition.

### Content bridge

Keep IDs, schema versions, localization keys, references, and consumer reachability explicit. Reject rows that cannot be reached or safely retired. The evidence packet includes one source path, one data row or content key, one input/output example, and one stop condition.

### Save bridge

Persist only non-recomputable authored progress and processed IDs in the selected existing owner. Prove round trip before adding volume. The evidence packet includes one source path, one data row or content key, one input/output example, and one stop condition.

### Determinism bridge

Use keyed seeded inputs and stable ordering. Replay must agree on consequences, records, and prose selection across reload. The evidence packet includes one source path, one data row or content key, one input/output example, and one stop condition.

### Presentation bridge

Expose truthful state with keyboard/controller focus, text equivalents, lifecycle disposal, and readable long-text behavior. The evidence packet includes one source path, one data row or content key, one input/output example, and one stop condition.

### Release bridge

Package the slice as a bounded handoff with premise evidence, focused checks, performance notes, rollback, and explicit unresolved decisions. The evidence packet includes one source path, one data row or content key, one input/output example, and one stop condition.

Every scene has an entry condition, choice, failure or refusal, concrete consequence, archive/journal fact, and late-arrival line. Keep prose restrained and sensory, with the mechanic and data contract carrying systemic meaning. The review names the smallest observable player result and the exact evidence that would prove it. If the source differs, keep the entry as a tagged proposal and stop at the boundary instead of compensating with a parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Verification and implementation handoff

This pass closes one loop and leaves a truthful question open. The acceptance packet must include a source path, an example involving the accord, an unresolved question, and a rollback boundary. Require premise evidence, focused data or contract checks, runtime smoke only when needed, save round trip, deterministic replay where applicable, performance notes, and rollback. A complete document is not an implementation receipt. The review names the smallest observable player result and the exact evidence that would prove it. If the source differs, keep the entry as a tagged proposal and stop at the boundary instead of compensating with a parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

**Pass 31 receipt:** Meridian Dawn Council is planning-complete when all ten fields have evidence, owner, player result, failure behavior, and open questions.

## Twelve new story and side-quest packets

### Story packet 25: The Sanction Bell

A bell announces a sanction before the sealed letter arrives. The player can soften the public line, enforce it, or ask who will carry the cost. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

Two factions bring damaged tools as evidence. The player must decide whether repair is apology, repayment, or a new obligation. ## Ten Wave 3 integration bridges

### Campaign bridge

Read current campaign flags and emit one named content fact; never add a second clock or victory state. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Faction bridge

Route consequences for Ash Meridian Compact, Glass Orchard Syndicate, Quiet Foundry League, Long-Wake Assembly, Sable Relay, and the proposed Meridian Assembly through the canonical standing or diplomacy authority after ID and alias review. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Relationship bridge

Read trust, affinity, grief, consent, and decay from existing survivor owners; a scene beat is not a relationship ledger. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Map/route bridge

Project Meridian Exchange, Glass Orchard cisterns, Quiet Foundry Hall, Long-Wake signal yard, Sable Relay steps onto current cartography, expedition, weather, vehicle, colony, and route seams rather than creating a parallel graph. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Shelter bridge

Use current facility, expansion, water, power, needs, duty, archive, celebration, and memorial owners. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Content bridge

Validate schema, IDs, localization keys, references, reachability, and retirement before adding volume. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Save bridge

Capture only non-recomputable progress or processed IDs in an existing owner and prove round trip. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Determinism bridge

Use keyed seeded inputs and stable ordering; paired replay must match outcomes and records after reload. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### UI bridge

Expose truthful state with focus, controller, text equivalents, disposal, and bounded loading; panels stay adapters. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Handoff bridge

Attach source paths, data examples, focused checks, performance notes, rollback, and unresolved decisions. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Deepening packet 1: mediation protocol cards

Mediation protocol cards is treated as a compact content and systems packet. Start with a current-source census: locate the owner, public API, catalog row, event producer, save section, host binding, and any existing plan claim. Define the player-facing loop in six beats: prepare, inspect, choose, commit, receive feedback, and decide what to do next. Give the packet one named mechanic, one location or shelter image, one character or faction voice, one failure state, and one late-game callback. Every packet is a proposal until its current owner, catalog reference, consumer, save seam, and host route are proven. It should state what the player sees, what can fail, and which existing fact is authoritative. It may enrich a journal, archive, radio, or epilogue surface, but it may not create a parallel ledger or a hidden authority. Candidate data uses schema_version, stable snake_case IDs, explicit references, localization keys, fallback text, and retirement notes. Stateful records are minimal, deterministic, migration-aware, and tested through focused round trips. UI copy names the action, cost, uncertainty, and irreversible consequence, with keyboard/controller focus and text alternatives. Performance is bounded by catalog parse, query, panel refresh, and long-text budgets; an optional content packet can be disabled without corrupting canonical state. The packet closes with a premise question, a source path to verify, a small input/output example, and a rollback boundary.

The fiction remains material and specific: soot in a seal groove, wet chalk under a glove, a meal cooling while two people argue, a lamp reflected in a chart, or a name written twice because both versions are true. That texture is connected to a mechanic, a location, a faction memory, or a consequence so the prose adds playable meaning. A scene can end in refusal, delay, repair, compromise, or a clean break; each result is legible and archived by the owner that actually changed. The packet must not claim the mediation protocol cards already exists, and it must stop if a current system or approved plan already owns the behavior.

The fiction remains material and specific: soot in a seal groove, wet chalk under a glove, a meal cooling while two people argue, a lamp reflected in a chart, or a name written twice because both versions are true. That texture is connected to a mechanic, a location, a faction memory, or a consequence so the prose adds playable meaning. A scene can end in refusal, delay, repair, compromise, or a clean break; each result is legible and archived by the owner that actually changed. The packet must not claim the shared patrol debriefs already exists, and it must stop if a current system or approved plan already owns the behavior.

### Deepening packet 10: Meridian Assembly charter language

Meridian assembly charter language is treated as a compact content and systems packet. Start with a current-source census: locate the owner, public API, catalog row, event producer, save section, host binding, and any existing plan claim. Define the player-facing loop in six beats: prepare, inspect, choose, commit, receive feedback, and decide what to do next. Give the packet one named mechanic, one location or shelter image, one character or faction voice, one failure state, and one late-game callback. Every packet is a proposal until its current owner, catalog reference, consumer, save seam, and host route are proven. It should state what the player sees, what can fail, and which existing fact is authoritative. It may enrich a journal, archive, radio, or epilogue surface, but it may not create a parallel ledger or a hidden authority. Candidate data uses schema_version, stable snake_case IDs, explicit references, localization keys, fallback text, and retirement notes. Stateful records are minimal, deterministic, migration-aware, and tested through focused round trips. UI copy names the action, cost, uncertainty, and irreversible consequence, with keyboard/controller focus and text alternatives. Performance is bounded by catalog parse, query, panel refresh, and long-text budgets; an optional content packet can be disabled without corrupting canonical state. The packet closes with a premise question, a source path to verify, a small input/output example, and a rollback boundary.

The fiction remains material and specific: soot in a seal groove, wet chalk under a glove, a meal cooling while two people argue, a lamp reflected in a chart, or a name written twice because both versions are true. That texture is connected to a mechanic, a location, a faction memory, or a consequence so the prose adds playable meaning. A scene can end in refusal, delay, repair, compromise, or a clean break; each result is legible and archived by the owner that actually changed. The packet must not claim the Meridian Assembly charter language already exists, and it must stop if a current system or approved plan already owns the behavior.

## Wave 3 dense-volume handoff

The ten deepening packets are ready for premise review as a high-volume authoring backlog. A builder should select one packet only after proving the current seam, then implement the smallest vertical slice with one canonical result, one visible route, one persistence or projection check, and one deterministic replay case where state changes. Writers may continue expanding the voice and location banks, but every new line needs a consumer, trigger, localization key, and archive policy.


## Continuation Wave 4 — Passes 32–42: Ash Meridian Diplomacy and Late-Game Coalition

This fourth synchronized tranche extends the ten existing fields with new mechanics, systems, locations, lore, character material, factions, and late-game consequences. Fields 11–20 remain deferred until this individual plan reaches 100,000 words. The material is documentation-only, premise-gated, and bounded by DiplomaticSummitSystem, canonical faction standing, relationship and radio owners, CampaignState, ShelterArchiveSystem, and quest routing.

## Wave 4 micro-variant bank

These short records raise prose volume while keeping each addition reviewable and tied to an owner.

### Micro-variant 1: quiet clause variants

Quiet clause variants is a six-line variant family for the current Wave 4 content. This micro-bank supplies six short variants for calm, pressure, loss, recovery, refusal, and late arrival. Each line receives a localization key, speaker or surface, trigger, and fallback. The variant points to one existing mechanic or fact and names the consequence in plain language. It may change tone, public memory, or a next available choice, but it cannot mutate a second ledger. The writer keeps the material details close: a dry seal, a wet glove, a meal left under cloth, a lamp turned low, a tool returned, or a name spoken twice. The systems note identifies the canonical owner, the UI note identifies focus and text alternatives, and the verification note identifies one focused check and one reload case. It remains provisional until the source census proves that the referenced route, faction, survivor, location, archive, and save seams are live and unique.

### Story packet 49: The Constitution Scrap

## Ten Wave 5 integration bridges

### Campaign bridge

Read current campaign flags and emit one named content fact; never add a second clock or victory state. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Faction bridge

Route consequences for Ash Meridian Compact, Glass Orchard Syndicate, Quiet Foundry League, Long-Wake Assembly, Sable Relay, and Meridian Assembly through canonical standing or diplomacy after ID and alias review. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Relationship bridge

Read trust, affinity, grief, consent, and decay from existing survivor owners; a scene beat is not a relationship ledger. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Map/route bridge

Project Meridian Exchange, Glass Orchard cisterns, Quiet Foundry Hall, Long-Wake signal yard, Sable Relay steps onto current cartography, expedition, weather, vehicle, colony, and route seams rather than creating a parallel graph. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Shelter bridge

Use current facility, expansion, water, power, needs, duty, archive, celebration, and memorial owners. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Content bridge

Validate schema, IDs, localization keys, references, reachability, and retirement before adding volume. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Save bridge

Capture only non-recomputable progress or processed IDs in an existing owner and prove round trip. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Determinism bridge

Use keyed seeded inputs and stable ordering; paired replay must match outcomes and records after reload. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### UI bridge

## Continuation Wave 6 — Passes 54–64: Ash Meridian Diplomacy and Late-Game Coalition

Wave 6 continues after the post-100k field layer. The active top-level structure is now twenty fields, while each pass below revisits the original ten operational fields and cross-references the new layer.

### Pass 54: Coalition Census

#### Canon and premise delta

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. The premise audit must prove whether the seal already exists under another name before this proposal advances. Recheck current source, data, save ownership, host construction, and live ledger claims. Existing APIs and catalogs outrank this proposal. If a current owner supplies the behavior, retain this as content, projection, or presentation. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Player loop and decision pressure

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. Use the witness as the player-facing review object and connect it to one of Fields 11–20 without inventing a new store. Describe preparation, inspection, commitment, feedback, and the next decision. Name cost and refusal. Use canonical day, resource, needs, travel, relationship, faction, and campaign facts rather than hidden local counters. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### New mechanic and system rules

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. The focal mechanic is coalition census derived from current standing and treaty facts. Define inputs, thresholds, mutation owner, failure response, and visible feedback. State inputs, thresholds, evaluation order, consequence, no-provider behavior, and one mutation owner. Keyed seeded variation must be stable. Consumers receive facts and cannot become authorities. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Locations and shelter lore

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. Anchor the scene in the envoy: describe sound, material, work, hazard, shelter meaning, and map or facility seam. Give the place material texture, practical job, hazard, shelter relation, and memory. New IDs remain candidate POIs until map and facility owners confirm them. A vignette must lead to clue, choice, record, or route. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Character and faction continuity

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. Give one character a reason to protect the accord, another a reason to question it, and a faction a reason to remember it. Give each voice desire, limit, rhythm, and change. Read roster, relationship, standing, skill, memorial, and campaign facts. Proposed factions require alias and standing-sink checks. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Authored data and prose schema

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. Candidate rows must name the clause with stable IDs, trigger, references, fallback text, localization, and archive policy. Candidate rows need schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, and retirement notes. High-volume rows reject dangling references. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Persistence and deterministic replay

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. If the seal recurs, specify minimal progress or processed-event state and keyed replay inputs that prevent duplicates. Persist only non-recomputable progress and processed events in an existing owner. Specify capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event, rollback. Replay must agree on outcomes, records, order, and prose keys. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Host/UI/UX and performance

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. The player must find the witness, understand state, navigate with keyboard/controller, and receive a safe fallback if data is absent or large. Expose truthful state with focus-safe keyboard/controller navigation, text alternatives, contrast, long-text behavior, disposal, and bounded query/load budgets. Panels stay adapters. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Storyline and side-quest consequences

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. Stage a short scene around the rumor, with a quiet prose beat, practical choice, and consequence routed through an existing owner. Every scene needs entry condition, choice, refusal or failure, concrete consequence, archive/journal fact, and late-arrival line. Keep prose restrained and sensory. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Verification and implementation handoff

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. The acceptance packet must include a source path, input/output example involving the envoy, unresolved question, and rollback boundary. Require premise evidence, focused data or contract checks, runtime smoke only when needed, save round trip, deterministic replay, performance notes, and rollback. A document is not implementation. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

## Ten Wave 6 integration bridges

### Campaign bridge

Read current campaign flags and emit one named content fact; never add a second clock or victory state. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Faction bridge

Route consequences for Ash Meridian Compact, Glass Orchard Syndicate, Quiet Foundry League, Long-Wake Assembly, Sable Relay, and Meridian Assembly through canonical standing or diplomacy after ID and alias review. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Relationship bridge

Read trust, affinity, grief, consent, and decay from existing survivor owners; a scene beat is not a relationship ledger. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Map/route bridge

Project Meridian Exchange, Glass Orchard cisterns, Quiet Foundry Hall, Long-Wake signal yard, Sable Relay steps onto current cartography, expedition, weather, vehicle, colony, and route seams rather than creating a parallel graph. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Shelter bridge

Use current facility, expansion, water, power, needs, duty, archive, celebration, and memorial owners. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Content bridge

Validate schema, IDs, localization keys, references, reachability, and retirement before adding volume. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Save bridge

Capture only non-recomputable progress or processed IDs in an existing owner and prove round trip. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Determinism bridge

Use keyed seeded inputs and stable ordering; paired replay must match outcomes and records after reload. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### UI bridge

Expose truthful state with focus, controller, text equivalents, disposal, and bounded loading; panels stay adapters. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Handoff bridge

Attach source paths, data examples, focused checks, performance notes, rollback, and unresolved decisions. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

## Ten Wave 7 integration bridges

### Campaign bridge

Read current campaign flags and emit one named content fact; never add a second clock or victory state. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Faction bridge

Route consequences for Ash Meridian Compact, Glass Orchard Syndicate, Quiet Foundry League, Long-Wake Assembly, Sable Relay, and Meridian Assembly through canonical standing or diplomacy after ID and alias review. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Relationship bridge

Read trust, affinity, grief, consent, and decay from existing survivor owners; a scene beat is not a relationship ledger. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Map/route bridge

Project Meridian Exchange, Glass Orchard cisterns, Quiet Foundry Hall, Long-Wake signal yard, Sable Relay steps onto current cartography, expedition, weather, vehicle, colony, and route seams rather than creating a parallel graph. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Shelter bridge

Use current facility, expansion, water, power, needs, duty, archive, celebration, and memorial owners. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Content bridge

Validate schema, IDs, localization keys, references, reachability, and retirement before adding volume. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Save bridge

Capture only non-recomputable progress or processed IDs in an existing owner and prove round trip. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Determinism bridge

Use keyed seeded inputs and stable ordering; paired replay must match outcomes and records after reload. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### UI bridge

Expose truthful state with focus, controller, text equivalents, disposal, and bounded loading; panels stay adapters. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Handoff bridge

Attach source paths, data examples, focused checks, performance notes, rollback, and unresolved decisions. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Volume packet 01: The Bellmaker’s Table

This dense Wave 7 continuation packet extends Ash Meridian through a contested promise and a choice between public repair, private repair, or a principled refusal. It is deliberately additive: it does not create another field layer after Fields 11–20, and it does not claim that a provisional faction, location, mechanic, or prose record exists in production.

Place the first clue near a practical tool: a pump handle, route chalk, ration tin, needle, relay key, or ledger clasp. The object teaches the mechanic through use.

The playable beat begins with a short observation at the ash meridian seam. A resident asks a question that cannot be answered by a tooltip alone. The player can inspect the evidence, ask for the practical need, compare two records, or leave the matter untouched. Inspection grants context; asking exposes a cost; comparison reveals a mismatch; leaving preserves uncertainty. The command must be represented by an existing owner event and must emit a fact that later systems can consume without reading panel state.

The scene then crosses three scales. At shelter scale, one room or work area changes its arrangement and writes a small archive or journal result. At faction scale, one representative revises a stance, makes a concession, or names a boundary. At late-game scale, the same fact appears as a route, legacy, coalition, or ending input. These projections are read-only views of canonical state. They must degrade gracefully when the optional record is missing and must never invent a favorable outcome merely to complete the prose.

Character direction for this packet: the practical resident speaks in short sentences, notices tools before symbols, and offers help without promising safety. The faction voice uses formal language until challenged by a concrete shortage. A third voice, perhaps a courier, apprentice, witness, or absent person represented by an object, reframes the conflict. Their personalities are differentiated through choices and timing rather than accent caricature. Give each voice a refusal that can be respected and a late callback that acknowledges the player’s earlier decision.

Location and shelter lore should answer who built the space, what failed, who repaired it, what rule grew from that repair, and what the rule costs now. Use one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. The place becomes more than a backdrop because the player can act there, return there, and observe a consequence there. Do not duplicate a named location: run a catalog and alias check and fold into an existing record if the premise is already covered.

Mechanic acceptance for The Bellmaker’s Table: a focused owner check proves the command and event; a save round trip proves capture and restore; a paired seeded replay proves order and result; a bounded host smoke proves the projection; and a UI review proves focus, close/back, contrast, text scaling, and long-copy behavior. Performance review records catalog parse, query, refresh, and archive costs. The rollback note identifies the event key, record IDs, migration boundary, and prose keys that can be removed without orphaning live state.

The packet closes with a quiet image: place the first clue near a practical tool: a pump handle, route chalk, ration tin, needle, relay key, or ledger clasp. the object teaches the mechanic through use. The image is not a reward screen. It is a check that the player’s choice has entered the world’s ordinary labor. If the source owner, data schema, or current integration plan disagrees with this proposal, retain the packet as a bounded question and stop at the premise audit rather than creating a parallel system.

### Pass 76: The Rainline Witness

This pass extends Ash Meridian diplomacy with the rainline witness. ### Supplemental packet 01: Ash Meridian diplomacy — Copper Meridian Hall action 1

The scene opens at **Copper Meridian Hall**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Copper Meridian Hall, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Night Orchard Delegation** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The packet is not an implementation claim; it is ready only for a safe-slice review.

## Wave 13 closeout receipt

The Wave 13 material remains documentation-only. Promotion requires current-source premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, reachable data, deterministic save and replay fixtures, UI/accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary.

## Wave 13 supplemental depth packets

These packets add volume to the current Wave 13 fields without introducing Fields 21–30. Each is a bounded design record for story, mechanics, systems, locations, shelter lore, character personalities, factions, late-game pressure, UI, persistence, replay, and performance.


### Supplemental packet 01: Ash Meridian diplomacy — Pale River House action 1

The scene opens at **Pale River House**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Pale River House, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Pale River Envoys** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The packet is not an implementation claim; it is ready only for a safe-slice review.

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at Glassroot Gallery. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

Write distinct voices for a practical resident, an affected witness, and one representative of Glassroot Covenant. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, refusal, apology, and late callback. Let a minor or absent voice receive a measurable consequence.

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

Provide concise labels, expanded explanations, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, contrast, text scaling, non-color cues, irreversible-action confirmation, and a text or audio alternative. Long records must page or collapse without hiding the consequence.

#### 10. Performance and rollback

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, panel refresh, archive projection, and long text. Include a missing-data path, a rollback boundary, a focused contract check, a save round trip, and a host smoke only where the owner route requires it.
**Pass 174 receipt.** Accept The Mended Seal only when the owner, player result, failure behavior, save/replay fixture, and rollback note are written. The prose beat ends with an ordinary action: a lamp is trimmed, a pump is checked, a meal is shared, a coat is mended, a route marker is moved, or a record is read aloud. If that action cannot be wired to current authority, keep the packet as a design question.

## Wave 16 closeout receipt

The Wave 16 material remains documentation-only. Promotion requires current-source premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, reachable data, deterministic save and replay fixtures, UI/accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary.

## Wave 16 supplemental depth packets

These packets add volume to the current Wave 16 fields without introducing Fields 21–30. Each is a bounded design record for story, mechanics, systems, locations, shelter lore, character personalities, factions, late-game pressure, UI, persistence, replay, and performance.


### Supplemental packet 01: Ash Meridian diplomacy — Dawn Kettle House action 1

The scene opens at **Dawn Kettle House**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Dawn Kettle House, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Dawn Kettle Delegates** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The packet is not an implementation claim; it is ready only for a safe-slice review.

### Pass 197: The Frostline Witness

This pass extends Ash Meridian diplomacy with the frostline witness. It is a proposal over the current authority owned by DiplomaticSummitSystem, canonical faction standing, relationship, radio, campaign, ShelterArchiveSystem, and quest owners. The named factions and places are provisional labels, not catalog facts. Start with a source, data, consumer, and ownership audit; if an existing record already expresses the idea, fold this material into that record or stop. The player should make a legible choice that affects a practical task, a remembered relationship, a route, or a late-game interpretation.

#### 1. Premise evidence

Record the exact source path, API or JSON family, event producer, host route, and current plan entry that justify the frostline witness. Name one absent seam and one collision to check. A proposal remains tagged unresolved until the premise is reproduced against current source.

#### 2. Owner contract

Route the command through DiplomaticSummitSystem, canonical faction standing, relationship, radio, campaign, ShelterArchiveSystem, and quest owners. Define the input, output, refusal, fallback, and event key. Panels, maps, and prose consume the projection and never become a second ledger, graph, clock, route registry, roster, or ending resolver.

#### 3. Player action

Give the player inspect, ask, compare, repair, invite, ration, disclose, wait, or leave choices around the frostline witness. Show cost before commitment, allow a respectful refusal, and provide recovery work or information after a failure unless the canonical owner defines a terminal outcome.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at Brass Wren House. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

Write distinct voices for a practical resident, an affected witness, and one representative of Brass Wren Envoys. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, refusal, apology, and late callback. Let a minor or absent voice receive a measurable consequence.

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

Provide concise labels, expanded explanations, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, contrast, text scaling, non-color cues, irreversible-action confirmation, and a text or audio alternative. Long records must page or collapse without hiding the consequence.

#### 10. Performance and rollback

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, panel refresh, archive projection, and long text. Include a missing-data path, a rollback boundary, a focused contract check, a save round trip, and a host smoke only where the owner route requires it.
